newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude EFPs remain at premium to NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude EFPs remain at premium to NYMEX.

text.p: Sluggish cash crude markets maintained a premium to NYMEX paper contracts Wednesday, with July Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) garnering attention at 13-15 cents over July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing paper.
Outright July WTI/Cushing talked late at $20.65-75 a barrel, moving five cents lower on marginally bearish American Petroleum Institute (API) stock data.
API numbers showed crude stocks building 1.4 million barrels for week-ended May 23, with gasoline stocks down 1.12 million barrels and distillates 3.32 million barrels higher.
Domestic grade markets were stalled by the lack of refiner demand for July barrels, and the absence of players, still holding-out after the long weekend holiday, traders said.
Midland/WTI sold at 35 cents under benchmark WTI, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James done at minus six and seven cents and West Texas Sour/Midland at marker -$1.53.
WTI/Cushing Postings were steady at deals from $1.95-$1.97, traders said.
EFPs extended their premium to outright WTI. Refiners weary of getting stuck with unwanted foreign barrels at delivery time kept EFPs solidly firm against paper.
